fields.label: crowncarpet
fields.description: A fuzzy, rainbow-banded sheet of thermophile bacteria and algae that carpets the margins of any ocean warm enough to host it — rare on an ordinary shore, thick and unbroken where the water boils. It is some of the oldest life on any planet, wearing the loudest colors: the shore's one truth that never lies about the heat. Pressed while still fresh, it yields Deepfire, a pigment that glows.

fields.label: fresh crowncarpet

fields.label: deepfire

fields.label: deepfire press

fields.label: deepfire worn light (internal)

fields.label: glowtank
fields.description: A squat glass-and-iron vat that cultures crowncarpet from a seed of the fresh mat. Slow and low-yield compared to a wild shore, but it needs no ocean — only power, a seed, and patience.

fields.label: deepfire dish
fields.description: A fine meal finished with a spoonful of deepfire pigment. It tingles going down, and it never wears off.
